note if the density is relatively equal or significantly asymmetric.", "Determine the vertical zonal distribution by dividing the lungs into upper, mid, and lower zones; identify where the consolidation is most dense (e.g., mid-to-lower zone predominance vs. upper lobe predominance).", "Evaluate the cardiac silhouette size and costophrenic angles to check for cardiomegaly or pleural effusions, which would suggest hydrostatic edema rather than non-cardiogenic causes.", "Inspect the texture of the opacities to distinguish between fluffy air-space disease (alveolar filling) and reticular/honeycombing patterns (interstitial fibrosis)."]}]

B) A 3cm round, non-enhancing lesion located in the right upper lobe pulmonary artery.
C) A 3cm round, enhancing lesion located in the right middle lobe pulmonary artery.
D) A 3cm irregular, enhancing lesion located in the left upper lobe pulmonary artery.
E) A 3cm round, enhancing lesion located in the left lower lobe pulmonary artery.
